questions.q: According to the Chief Electoral Officer of Meghalaya, how are the State's 60 Assembly constituencies distributed between the Khasi–Jaintia Hills and Garo Hills divisions?
questions.e: The CEO Meghalaya profile gives 36 constituencies for the Khasi and Jaintia Hills division and 24 for the Garo Hills division. The figures add to the State total of 60.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Meghalaya — About Us.

questions.sourceName: Office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Meghalaya — About Us

questions.q: How many constituencies does Meghalaya have for election to the Lok Sabha, according to the State's official government profile?
questions.e: The Meghalaya Government and CEO Meghalaya profiles list two House of the People (Lok Sabha) constituencies. This is the State's parliamentary representation in the directly elected House.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Meghalaya — About Us.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Meghalaya — About Us

questions.q: The official Meghalaya election profile lists how many seats for the State in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha)?
questions.e: The CEO Meghalaya profile lists one Council of States constituency for Meghalaya. Do not confuse this with its two Lok Sabha constituencies.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Meghalaya — About Us.

questions.q: Under the Meghalaya Government's description of district administration, who is the head of a district administration?
questions.e: The Meghalaya Government portal identifies the Deputy Commissioner as the head of the district administration. The DC coordinates district-level administration and performs executive, revenue and magisterial functions assigned by law.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Meghalaya Government Portal — Shillong District Administrative Setup.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Meghalaya Government Portal — Shillong District Administrative Setup

questions.q: According to the Government of Meghalaya's Vision 2030 document, approximately how long is the State's international boundary with Bangladesh?
questions.e: The Government-commissioned Meghalaya Vision 2030 document states that Meghalaya shares a 443-kilometre international border with Bangladesh along its south and southwest. The earlier 423-kilometre figure was incorrect and has been replaced after checking the source.

questions.q: According to the Chief Electoral Officer of Meghalaya, how many administrative divisions and districts does the State have?
questions.e: The CEO Meghalaya profile lists two divisions and eleven districts. It separately states that the Khasi and Jaintia Hills division has 36 Assembly constituencies and the Garo Hills division has 24.

questions.q: Which set correctly identifies the three types of urban local bodies contemplated by Article 243Q?
o: Gram Sabha, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad
Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council and Municipal Corporation
District Council, Regional Council and Village Council
Town Committee, Cantonment Board and Development Authority
questions.e: Article 243Q provides for a Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area, a Municipal Council for a smaller urban area and a Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area. The Governor specifies the relevant areas by public notification, subject to the constitutional criteria.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026

questions.q: Under Article 243R, the ordinary elected representatives of a Municipality are chosen from which territorial units?
questions.e: Article 243R provides for persons chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the municipal area. These constituencies are commonly called wards. The Constitution also permits specified representation of other persons, subject to the article.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026

questions.q: Under Article 243S, a Ward Committee is constitutionally required in a Municipality whose population is at least:
questions.e: Article 243S requires Ward Committees within the territorial area of a Municipality having a population of three lakh or more. State law determines their composition and territorial arrangements, subject to the constitutional provision.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026

questions.q: What minimum proportion of the total seats to be filled by direct election in every Municipality must be reserved for women under Article 243T?
questions.e: Article 243T requires not less than one-third of the total number of seats to be reserved for women, including the seats reserved for women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. State law may provide for a larger reservation.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026

questions.q: What is the normal constitutional duration of a Municipality under Article 243U, unless it is sooner dissolved?
questions.e: Article 243U fixes the normal duration of every Municipality at five years from the date appointed for its first meeting. An election to constitute the Municipality must ordinarily be completed before the expiry of that duration.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026

questions.topic: Article 243V — minimum age for municipal membership
questions.q: A person is otherwise qualified to contest a municipal election. Which statement about age is correct under Article 243V?
o: The person must be at least 18 years old
The person must be at least 21 years old
The person must be at least 25 years old
The Constitution sets no minimum age
questions.e: Article 243V provides that a person is not disqualified on the ground of age if the person has attained 21 years. A State law cannot make the minimum age for municipal membership 25 merely by importing the age requirement for membership of a State Legislative Assembly.
tags: Article 243V — minimum age for municipal membership
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026

questions.q: Which subject is expressly included in the Twelfth Schedule as a possible municipal function?
questions.e: The Twelfth Schedule includes urban planning, including town planning, among the matters that may be entrusted to Municipalities by State legislation under Article 243W. The list also covers matters such as roads, water supply and public health.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026

questions.q: Which statement best describes the power to levy municipal taxes under Article 243X?
o: Every Municipality may create any tax without State legislation
The State Legislature may by law authorise a Municipality to levy, collect and appropriate specified taxes, duties, tolls and fees
Only Parliament may authorise municipal taxes
Municipalities may levy income tax on all residents directly under the Constitution
questions.e: Article 243X enables the State Legislature to authorise Municipalities by law to levy, collect and appropriate specified taxes, duties, tolls and fees, subject to prescribed procedure and limits. The article does not give every Municipality an unlimited independent taxing power.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026

questions.q: Which body reviews the financial position of Municipalities under Article 243Y?
o: The Finance Commission constituted under Article 243-I
The Comptroller and Auditor General alone
questions.e: Article 243Y assigns the review of municipal finances to the Finance Commission constituted under Article 243-I. It makes recommendations to the Governor on distribution of resources, grants and measures needed to improve municipal finances.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026

questions.q: Article 243Z requires State legislation to make provision for which municipal-finance matter?
o: The accounts of Municipalities and their audit
The appointment of High Court judges
The conduct of Lok Sabha elections
The creation of a State Public Service Commission
questions.e: Article 243Z provides that the Legislature of a State may make provisions with respect to the maintenance of accounts by Municipalities and the auditing of those accounts. It is distinct from Article 243Y, which deals with the Finance Commission's review of municipal finances.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Legislative Department — Constitution of India, updated 20 May 2026

questions.q: Which option correctly completes this sentence using the expression 'had better': 'The clerk ___ the file today.'
o: The clerk had better to submit the file today.
The clerk had better submits the file today.
The clerk had better submit the file today.
The clerk had better submitted the file today.
questions.e: The expression 'had better' is followed by the bare infinitive, without 'to'. It gives strong advice about a specific present or future situation. Therefore, 'had better submit' is correct.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — Had better.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Cambridge Dictionary — Had better

questions.topic: Would rather with a different subject
questions.q: Choose the correct completion: 'The supervisor would rather the assistant ___ the register before leaving.'
questions.e: When 'would rather' expresses a preference about what another person does, it is commonly followed by a clause whose verb is in the past simple, although the meaning refers to the present or future. Thus 'the assistant checked' is correct.
tags: Would rather with a different subject
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — Prefer, would prefer and would rather.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Cambridge Dictionary — Prefer, would prefer and would rather

questions.q: Choose the pronoun that correctly completes the formal relative clause: 'The candidate ___ the committee invited has accepted the post.'
questions.e: In the relative clause 'the committee invited ___', the pronoun is the object of the verb 'invited'. 'Whom' is the objective form used for a person in formal written English; 'who' is the subject form.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — Relative pronouns.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Cambridge Dictionary — Relative pronouns

questions.q: A writer wants to join two closely related independent clauses without using a coordinating conjunction. Which punctuation mark is appropriate?
questions.e: A semicolon can join two closely related independent clauses when no coordinating conjunction is used. A comma alone would create a comma splice; an apostrophe and a hyphen do not perform this function.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — Punctuation.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Cambridge Dictionary — Punctuation

questions.topic: Colon — introducing an explanation or list
questions.q: A complete clause is followed by a list of three documents. Which punctuation mark is normally used to introduce the list?
questions.e: A colon may introduce a list after a complete independent clause. The clause before the colon should be grammatically complete; the list then supplies the details.
tags: Colon — introducing an explanation or list
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — Punctuation.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Cambridge Dictionary — Punctuation

questions.q: In the sentence 'The detailed annexure complements the main report', the word 'complements' means:
questions.e: 'Complement' means something that completes, improves or goes well with another thing. 'Compliment' means an expression of praise. The annexure enhances the report, so 'complements' is correct.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — Complement.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Cambridge Dictionary — Complement

questions.q: In the sentence 'All but two applications were verified', the phrase 'all but two' means:
o: Two applications in addition to all others
questions.e: 'All but two' means all except two. If there were 20 applications, 18 were verified and two were not. The phrase does not mean that only two were verified.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — All but.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Cambridge Dictionary — All but

questions.q: In official usage, 'The officer was authorised by virtue of the delegation order' means that the officer was authorised:
o: Because of or under the authority of the order
questions.e: 'By virtue of' means because of, or by the authority or force of, something. Here the delegation order is the legal or administrative basis for the officer's authority.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — By virtue of.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Cambridge Dictionary — By virtue of

questions.q: If the roots of x² − 7x + 12 = 0 are r and s, what is the value of r × s?
questions.e: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the product of the roots is c/a. Here a = 1 and c = 12, so rs = 12. Factorisation gives (x − 3)(x − 4) = 0, confirming the roots 3 and 4.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook and exemplar resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Mathematics textbook and exemplar resources

questions.q: The sequence 5, 8, 11, 14, … is an arithmetic progression. What is its 20th term?
questions.e: The first term a = 5 and common difference d = 3. The nth term is aₙ = a + (n − 1)d. Therefore a₂₀ = 5 + 19 × 3 = 5 + 57 = 62.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook and exemplar resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Mathematics textbook and exemplar resources

questions.q: An officer can use a free afternoon either to prepare an audit report or attend a training session. If she chooses to prepare the audit report, what is the opportunity cost?
o: The value of the training session she gives up
The salary already earned that month
The total value of both activities
The cost of stationery used for the report
questions.e: Opportunity cost is the value of the next-best alternative forgone when a choice is made. If the officer chooses the audit report, the training session is the next-best alternative sacrificed. It is not necessarily a cash payment.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Economics textbooks and learning resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Economics textbooks and learning resources

questions.q: A point on level ground is 30 metres from the foot of a vertical tower. If the angle of elevation of its top is 30°, what is the tower's height?
questions.e: For the right triangle, tan 30° = height/30. Since tan 30° = 1/√3, height = 30/√3 = 10√3 metres. The observer's eye level is assumed to be at ground level.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook and exemplar resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Mathematics textbook and exemplar resources

questions.q: The Meiji Restoration of 1868 in Japan is best described as:
o: The restoration of imperial political authority, followed by rapid state-led modernisation
The establishment of a communist government after the Second World War
The division of Japan into occupation zones after 1945
The abolition of all central government institutions
questions.e: The Meiji Restoration ended the Tokugawa shogunate's political dominance and restored governing authority to the emperor. The new leadership pursued rapid institutional, military, educational and industrial modernisation.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Class XI History, Themes in World History.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Class XI History, Themes in World History

questions.q: Deep-ocean thermohaline circulation is driven primarily by differences in seawater density caused by variations in:
questions.e: Thermohaline circulation is linked to density differences in seawater. Temperature and salinity both affect density: colder and generally saltier water is denser and can sink, helping drive large-scale deep-ocean circulation.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NOAA Ocean Service — Ocean circulation and currents.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NOAA Ocean Service — Ocean circulation and currents

questions.q: What is the solution set of the inequality |2x − 3| < 5?
questions.e: For |A| < b with b positive, write −b < A < b. Thus −5 < 2x − 3 < 5. Add 3 throughout: −2 < 2x < 8. Divide by 2: −1 < x < 4. Both endpoints are excluded because the original inequality is strict.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook and exemplar resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Mathematics textbook and exemplar resources

questions.q: In a typical covalent bond between two non-metal atoms, the atoms achieve bonding primarily by:
o: Sharing one or more pairs of electrons
questions.e: A covalent bond forms when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons. This differs from ionic bonding, in which electrons are transferred and oppositely charged ions attract one another.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Chemistry textbook resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Chemistry textbook resources

questions.q: What is the value of log₁₀ 1000?
questions.e: A logarithm asks for the exponent to which the base must be raised. Since 10³ = 1000, log₁₀ 1000 = 3.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook and exemplar resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Mathematics textbook and exemplar resources

questions.q: An ecological footprint is an indicator that estimates:
o: The biologically productive area needed to provide the resources a population uses and absorb specified wastes
The total number of species found in a forest
The depth of groundwater below a settlement
The amount of rainfall received by a region in one year
questions.e: An ecological footprint expresses human demand on biologically productive land and water. It estimates the area needed to supply resources and absorb certain wastes, using prevailing technology and resource-management practices.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Global Footprint Network — Ecological Footprint.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Global Footprint Network — Ecological Footprint

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes a process from a thread in a conventional operating system?
o: Every thread always has a separate address space from every other thread
Threads within the same process normally share the process address space, while separate processes have separate address spaces
A process is only a file stored on disk
questions.e: A process is an executing program with its own process resources and address space. Threads are execution paths within a process and normally share that process's address space and resources, while each thread has its own execution state such as registers and stack.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. University of Wisconsin — Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: University of Wisconsin — Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces

questions.topic: Calendar — day after a fixed interval
questions.q: If 1 January of a non-leap year is a Monday, what day of the week is 1 March of that year?
questions.e: January has 31 days and February has 28 days in a non-leap year. From 1 January to 1 March is 31 + 28 = 59 days. Since 59 leaves remainder 3 when divided by 7, move three weekdays forward from Monday: Thursday.
tags: Calendar — day after a fixed interval

questions.topic: Berlin Conference — colonial claims in Africa
questions.q: The Berlin Conference of 1884–1885 is historically significant mainly because it:
o: Established rules among European powers for asserting colonial claims in Africa
Granted independence to all African colonies
questions.e: The Berlin Conference formalised principles and procedures by which European powers notified and recognised claims to territory in Africa. African rulers were not represented as equal participants, and the conference accelerated the Scramble for Africa rather than granting independence.
tags: Berlin Conference — colonial claims in Africa
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Berlin West Africa Conference.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Berlin West Africa Conference

questions.q: A correctly working analogue clock is seen in a plane mirror and appears to show 3:40. What is the actual time?
questions.e: For a standard 12-hour clock, actual time = 11:60 minus the mirror reading. Thus 11:60 − 3:40 = 8:20. This uses the mirror reversal of the clock face, not a change in elapsed time.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Original author-created logical reasoning problem.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Original author-created logical reasoning problem

questions.topic: Scheduling — identify the only feasible order
questions.q: Four files P, Q, R and S are processed one at a time. P is processed before R; S is processed immediately after Q; and R is processed last. Which order is possible?
questions.e: The pair Q–S must be consecutive and in that order. R must be last, and P must occur before R. Option B satisfies all three conditions: P first, Q immediately followed by S, and R last. The other options either reverse Q–S or break the immediate-adjacency condition.
tags: Scheduling — identify the only feasible order

questions.topic: French Revolution — fall of the Bastille
questions.q: The storming of the Bastille on 14 July 1789 became a symbol of the French Revolution primarily because the Bastille represented:
questions.e: The Bastille was a royal fortress-prison associated with the authority of the Bourbon monarchy. Its fall on 14 July 1789 became a powerful symbol of popular resistance to royal absolutism and is commemorated as France's national day.
tags: French Revolution — fall of the Bastille
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Encyclopaedia Britannica — French Revolution.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Encyclopaedia Britannica — French Revolution

questions.q: Which political group led the October Revolution in Russia in 1917?
questions.e: The Bolsheviks, led by Vladimir Lenin, organised the seizure of power in Petrograd in October 1917 according to the Russian calendar then in use. The event brought the Provisional Government to an end and led to Bolshevik rule.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Russian Revolution.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Russian Revolution

questions.q: The Treaty of Versailles of 1919 was the peace settlement imposed primarily on which country after the First World War?
questions.e: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in June 1919 between the Allied and Associated Powers and Germany. It imposed territorial, military and financial terms on Germany after the First World War.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Treaty of Versailles.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Treaty of Versailles

questions.q: The Industrial Revolution began first on a large scale in which country?
questions.e: The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain in the eighteenth century. Factors included access to coal and iron, capital, markets, transport improvements and technological innovation in textile production and steam power.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Industrial Revolution.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Industrial Revolution

questions.q: The European Renaissance first developed prominently in which region?
questions.e: The Renaissance began prominently in the Italian city-states, including Florence, Venice and Rome. Wealth from commerce, classical learning and patronage of artists and scholars helped its development before it spread across Europe.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Renaissance.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Renaissance

questions.q: The Reign of Terror in revolutionary France is most closely associated with the leadership of:
questions.e: The Reign of Terror (1793–1794) is closely associated with the Committee of Public Safety and the dominance of Maximilien Robespierre. Revolutionary tribunals and executions were used against people regarded as enemies of the revolution.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Reign of Terror.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Reign of Terror

questions.q: The Congress of Vienna (1814–1815) primarily sought to:
o: Restore a balance of power in Europe after the Napoleonic Wars
Unify Germany under a republican constitution
questions.e: The Congress of Vienna sought to restore political stability and a balance of power after Napoleon's defeat. It restored or rearranged monarchies and territories and promoted the principle of legitimacy among Europe's ruling dynasties.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Congress of Vienna.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Congress of Vienna

questions.q: In which year did the thirteen American colonies adopt the Declaration of Independence?
questions.e: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776. It announced the colonies' separation from British rule; the war continued until the Treaty of Paris in 1783 recognised American independence.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. U.S. National Archives — Declaration of Independence transcript.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: U.S. National Archives — Declaration of Independence transcript

questions.q: A river system whose tributaries join the main river at irregular acute angles, resembling the branches of a tree, is called:
questions.e: A dendritic drainage pattern resembles the branching structure of a tree. It commonly develops where the underlying rock has relatively uniform resistance and there is no strong structural control directing streams.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Geography textbooks and learning resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Geography textbooks and learning resources

questions.q: A drainage pattern with long parallel main streams and short tributaries joining at nearly right angles is known as:
questions.e: A trellis pattern commonly develops in folded or alternating resistant and less-resistant rock structures. Main streams follow valleys while short tributaries descend from adjacent ridges and join at near-right angles.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Geography textbooks and learning resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Geography textbooks and learning resources

questions.q: Spring tides generally occur when the Sun, Moon and Earth are:
o: At right angles, producing the smallest tidal range
Aligned, producing a larger tidal range
At their greatest distance from one another
In the same orbit around Earth
questions.e: Spring tides occur near new moon and full moon, when the gravitational effects of the Sun and Moon reinforce one another. This produces a larger tidal range, with higher high tides and lower low tides than usual.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NOAA Ocean Service — Tides and spring-neap cycles.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NOAA Ocean Service — Tides and spring-neap cycles

questions.q: A long, streamlined ridge carved by wind abrasion in an arid region is called a:
questions.e: A yardang is an elongated ridge formed mainly by wind erosion, with its long axis commonly aligned with the prevailing wind. It is characteristic of arid and semi-arid environments.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Yardang.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Yardang

questions.q: Laterite soils commonly develop in regions with high temperature and heavy rainfall because of:
o: Intense leaching of silica and bases, leaving iron and aluminium oxides
questions.e: High temperature and heavy rainfall promote intense chemical weathering and leaching. Silica and soluble bases are removed, while iron and aluminium oxides become relatively concentrated, giving lateritic soils their characteristic properties.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Geography textbooks and learning resources.

questions.q: On a map with a scale of 1:50,000, a straight-line distance of 2 cm represents what ground distance?
questions.e: A scale of 1:50,000 means 1 cm on the map represents 50,000 cm on the ground, or 500 m. Therefore 2 cm represents 1,000 m, which is 1 km.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Geography textbooks and learning resources.

questions.q: A sudden break in the longitudinal profile of a river, often appearing as a step or steep reach, is called a:
questions.e: A knickpoint is an abrupt change in a river's gradient. It may form after tectonic uplift, a change in base level or other disturbances, and can migrate upstream as the river adjusts its profile.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Geography textbooks and learning resources.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: The continental shelf is best described as:
o: The deep, flat floor of the ocean basin
The gently sloping submerged extension of a continent before the continental slope
A trench formed at a convergent plate boundary
questions.e: The continental shelf is the shallow, gently sloping submerged margin of a continent. It extends from the shoreline to the shelf break, beyond which the continental slope descends more steeply toward the deep ocean basin.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NOAA Ocean Service — Continental shelf.

questions.q: Which pair of characteristics best defines a pure public good?
questions.e: A pure public good is non-rival in consumption and non-excludable. One person's use does not substantially reduce availability to others, and it is difficult or costly to prevent people from benefiting. National defence is a standard example.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Economics textbooks and learning resources.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A factory pollutes a river, imposing health costs on nearby residents that are not included in the factory's production cost. This is an example of:
questions.e: A negative externality occurs when an activity imposes costs on third parties that are not reflected in the market price. The pollution creates a social cost beyond the private cost borne by the factory.

questions.q: If the government fixes a legally binding maximum price below the market equilibrium price, what is the likely immediate result, other things being equal?
questions.e: A price ceiling below equilibrium makes the good cheaper for buyers, increasing quantity demanded, while suppliers are willing to provide less at the lower price. Quantity demanded therefore exceeds quantity supplied, creating a shortage.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Economics textbooks and learning resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Economics textbooks and learning resources

questions.q: When demand is relatively more inelastic than supply, which side of the market generally bears the larger share of a per-unit tax burden?
o: The tax burden is always split equally
questions.e: The less elastic side of a market has fewer options to avoid the tax and therefore bears a larger share of its economic burden. If demand is more inelastic than supply, consumers generally bear more of the tax through a higher price.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Economics textbooks and learning resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Economics textbooks and learning resources

questions.q: A Gini coefficient of zero represents:
o: Equal tax rates for all households
questions.e: The Gini coefficient measures inequality. A value of zero represents perfect equality, while a value approaching one (or 100 when expressed as a percentage) represents greater inequality. It is commonly derived from the Lorenz curve.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Economics textbooks and learning resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Economics textbooks and learning resources

questions.q: Compared with the Consumer Price Index, the GDP deflator covers:
o: Prices of all domestically produced final goods and services included in GDP
Only goods purchased by rural households
questions.e: The GDP deflator reflects prices of domestically produced final goods and services included in GDP. The CPI tracks the prices of a specified consumer basket and can include imported consumer goods, so their coverage differs.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics and Economics resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics and Economics resources

questions.q: Under a progressive income-tax structure, what happens to the average tax rate as taxable income rises through the relevant brackets?
o: It becomes zero above the highest bracket
questions.e: A progressive tax structure imposes a higher average tax rate as income increases. This is different from a proportional tax, where the average rate remains constant, and a regressive tax, where the average rate falls as income rises.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Economics textbooks and learning resources.

questions.q: Atoms of the same element that have different mass numbers but the same atomic number are called:
questions.e: Isotopes have the same number of protons, so they have the same atomic number, but different numbers of neutrons and therefore different mass numbers. For example, carbon-12 and carbon-14 are isotopes of carbon.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Biology textbook resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Biology textbook resources

questions.q: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 4 days. What fraction of the original sample remains after 12 days?
questions.e: Twelve days contain three half-lives: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. The remaining fraction is (1/2)³ = 1/8. Each half-life reduces the amount present by one-half of the amount remaining at that time.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Biology textbook resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Biology textbook resources

questions.q: When pure silicon is doped with a small amount of a trivalent impurity such as boron, the resulting semiconductor is generally:
o: n-type, with electrons as majority carriers
p-type, with holes as majority carriers
questions.e: A trivalent dopant has one fewer valence electron than silicon. This creates an acceptor level and leaves holes as the majority charge carriers, producing a p-type semiconductor.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Biology textbook resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Biology textbook resources

questions.q: Resonance occurs when a system is driven by a periodic force whose frequency is:
o: Close to the system's natural frequency
questions.e: Resonance occurs when the driving frequency is equal or close to a system's natural frequency. Energy transfer becomes especially effective and the amplitude of oscillation can become large, subject to damping.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Biology textbook resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Biology textbook resources

questions.q: A convex lens has a focal length of 0.5 metre. What is its power?
questions.e: Power P = 1/f when focal length is measured in metres. For a convex lens f = +0.5 m, so P = 1/0.5 = +2 dioptres. The positive sign denotes a converging lens.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Biology textbook resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Biology textbook resources

questions.q: During transcription in a typical eukaryotic cell, genetic information in DNA is copied into:
questions.e: Transcription uses a DNA template to synthesise RNA. In protein-coding gene expression, the resulting messenger RNA carries the coded information from DNA for translation at ribosomes.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Biology textbook resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Science and Biology textbook resources

questions.q: Which feature most clearly distinguishes adaptive immunity from innate immunity?
o: It is present only in plants
It is limited to physical barriers
questions.e: Adaptive immunity involves antigen-specific lymphocyte responses and can form memory cells. This allows a faster and stronger response when the same antigen is encountered again. Innate immunity provides rapid, non-specific defence.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Biology textbook resources.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.topic: Chemical kinetics — catalyst and activation energy
questions.q: A catalyst generally increases the rate of a chemical reaction because it:
o: Raises the activation energy of the reaction
Provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy
Changes the equilibrium constant at a fixed temperature
Increases the total amount of reactants present
questions.e: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy, so a greater fraction of collisions can lead to reaction at a given temperature. A catalyst is regenerated overall and does not change the equilibrium constant at a fixed temperature; it helps equilibrium be reached faster.
tags: Chemical kinetics — catalyst and activation energy

questions.q: In the Environmental Impact Assessment process, the scoping stage primarily determines:
o: The final tax rate for the project
The key environmental issues and Terms of Reference for detailed study
questions.e: Scoping identifies the significant environmental issues that require detailed assessment and frames the Terms of Reference for the EIA study. It helps focus the assessment on likely impacts rather than collecting unrelated information.

questions.q: Under the EIA Notification framework, public consultation is intended primarily to:
o: Obtain concerns and responses from affected people and other stakeholders
Determine the market price of project land
questions.e: Public consultation provides an opportunity to record concerns of locally affected people and other stakeholders. It is one component of the EIA appraisal process and does not itself grant environmental clearance.

questions.q: Which pollutant is the central subject of the Minamata Convention?
questions.e: The Minamata Convention is a global treaty to protect human health and the environment from anthropogenic emissions and releases of mercury and mercury compounds. Its measures address mercury supply, products, industrial processes, emissions, releases and waste.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Secretariat of the Minamata Convention on Mercury — About the Convention.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Secretariat of the Minamata Convention on Mercury — About the Convention

questions.q: The Basel Convention primarily regulates the transboundary movement and disposal of:
o: Hazardous wastes and certain other wastes
questions.e: The Basel Convention aims to protect human health and the environment against adverse effects from hazardous and other wastes. It establishes controls on transboundary movements, including prior informed consent procedures for covered shipments.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Basel Convention Secretariat — Text of the Convention.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Under an extended producer responsibility approach for e-waste, who bears specified responsibility for ensuring that end-of-life products are channelled for environmentally sound management?
o: The producer, as defined under the applicable rules
questions.e: Extended Producer Responsibility places defined obligations on producers for the environmentally sound management of products at end of life. India's E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 use an EPR framework administered through the prescribed system.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Central Pollution Control Board — E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.

questions.q: In a properly managed aerobic composting process, organic waste is decomposed mainly by:
o: Microorganisms in the presence of oxygen
questions.e: Aerobic composting relies on microorganisms that break down organic matter in the presence of oxygen. Adequate aeration, moisture and a suitable carbon-to-nitrogen balance help the process and reduce anaerobic odours.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. United States Environmental Protection Agency — Composting.

questions.q: Which set lists the four necessary Coffman conditions for a deadlock in an operating system?
o: Mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no pre-emption, circular wait
questions.e: The four necessary conditions are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no pre-emption and circular wait. A deadlock requires all four to hold simultaneously; breaking any one of them can prevent deadlock.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. University of Illinois Chicago — Operating Systems: Deadlocks.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: University of Illinois Chicago — Operating Systems: Deadlocks

questions.q: A relational table is in First Normal Form (1NF) when:
o: Every table has exactly one row
Each field contains an atomic value and repeating groups are removed
Every non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute
All tables contain the same number of columns
questions.e: First Normal Form requires each field to contain a single atomic value and avoids repeating groups or arrays within a field. Higher normal forms address additional dependency problems.

questions.q: In an SQL query that groups rows with GROUP BY, which clause is used to filter groups after aggregate values have been calculated?
questions.e: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping. HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY and can use aggregate expressions such as COUNT(*) or SUM(amount).

questions.q: After a full backup, an incremental backup normally copies:
o: Every file on the system again
Only data changed since the most recent backup of any type
Only data changed since the last full backup
Only files that have never been opened
questions.e: An incremental backup records changes since the most recent backup, whether full or incremental. It can save storage and backup time, but restoration may require the full backup and each subsequent incremental set.

questions.q: How many bits are used in an IPv4 address?
questions.e: An IPv4 address is 32 bits long and is commonly written as four decimal octets separated by dots, such as 192.0.2.1. IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses.

questions.q: What is the principal purpose of the BCC field in an email?
o: To hide the BCC recipients' addresses from other recipients
To mark the message as urgent
To prevent the sender from seeing the message
questions.e: BCC means blind carbon copy. Addresses placed in BCC are not displayed to ordinary recipients in the message header, which is useful when sending a message to a group without disclosing everyone's email address.

questions.q: Subject to the statutory exceptions, input tax credit on a motor vehicle for transportation of persons having an approved seating capacity of not more than 13 persons (including the driver) is generally:
o: Always available to every registered person
Available only when the vehicle is second-hand
Available only through the electronic cash ledger
questions.e: Section 17(5)(a) generally blocks ITC on specified motor vehicles for transportation of persons with approved seating capacity of not more than 13, including the driver. The Act provides exceptions, including specified further-supply, passenger-transport and driving-training uses; those facts must be checked before deciding a real claim.

questions.q: A registered person receives a works contract service for construction of an immovable property (other than plant or machinery) for its own use. What is the general ITC treatment under Section 17(5)(c)?
o: ITC is blocked, except where the input service is used for further supply of works contract service
ITC is allowed only if paid in cash
questions.e: Section 17(5)(c) blocks ITC on works contract services supplied for construction of immovable property, other than plant or machinery, except where the service is an input service for further supply of works contract service. The use and statutory definitions matter.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. India Code — Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (consolidated text, 11 June 2026).

questions.q: A business constructs an office building on its own account and capitalises the construction cost. Under Section 17(5)(d), ITC on goods or services used for this construction is generally:
o: Blocked, subject to the plant-or-machinery exception
Always available because the building is used for business
Available only for the first year
Available if the supplier is from another State
questions.e: Section 17(5)(d) generally blocks ITC on goods or services received for construction of immovable property on a taxable person's own account, even when used in the course or furtherance of business, except for plant or machinery. 'Construction' includes specified reconstruction, renovation, additions or alterations to the extent capitalised.

questions.topic: CGST Section 16(4) — general ITC time limit
questions.q: Under the general rule in Section 16(4) of the CGST Act, the time limit for taking ITC on an invoice or debit note is the 30th day of November following the end of the relevant financial year, or:
o: The date of the next monthly return, whichever is later
The date of furnishing the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier
The date of the supplier's audit, whichever is earlier
The end of the calendar year, whichever is later
questions.e: Section 16(4), as amended, sets the general deadline as 30 November following the end of the financial year to which the invoice or debit note pertains, or the date of furnishing the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier. Specified retrospective relief under subsections (5) and (6) is separate and must not be confused with the general rule.

questions.topic: CGST Section 18(1)(a) — stock ITC on becoming liable
questions.q: A person becomes liable for GST registration and applies for registration within 30 days of becoming liable. Subject to prescribed conditions, Section 18(1)(a) allows ITC on eligible inputs held in stock and inputs in semi-finished or finished goods held on:
o: The date of the first annual return
The day immediately preceding the date from which the person becomes liable to pay tax
The date of the first audit
Any date selected by the taxpayer
questions.e: Section 18(1)(a) provides a special credit entitlement for a person who applies for registration within 30 days of becoming liable and is granted registration. The relevant stock is measured on the day immediately preceding the date from which the person becomes liable to pay tax, subject to conditions and restrictions.

questions.topic: CGST Section 56 — interest on delayed refund
questions.q: Under Section 56 of the CGST Act, if an amount ordered to be refunded under Section 54(5) is not refunded within 60 days from receipt of the application, interest at a notified rate not exceeding what percentage is generally payable?
questions.e: Section 56 provides for interest at a rate not exceeding 6% where the refund is not made within 60 days of receipt of the application. A separate ceiling of 9% applies in the specified case of a refund arising from an order that has attained finality. Always check the applicable notification for the notified rate.

questions.q: According to RBI's NEFT and RTGS FAQs current in November 2026, which statement correctly distinguishes the two systems?
o: Both settle every payment individually in real time
NEFT processes transactions in batches, while RTGS settles transactions continuously on a transaction-by-transaction basis
RTGS processes payments only once a day
NEFT is available only during bank branch hours
questions.e: The RBI explains that NEFT processes transactions received up to a particular time in batches, whereas RTGS processes instructions continuously, transaction by transaction. NEFT and RTGS are both available round the clock, but their settlement mechanisms differ.

questions.q: According to the RBI RTGS FAQ updated on 14 October 2026, what is the minimum amount for an RTGS transfer and is there an RBI-set maximum ceiling?
questions.e: The RBI's RTGS FAQ states that the minimum amount is ₹2,00,000 and that there is no upper or maximum ceiling set by RBI. Banks may apply their own customer-facing arrangements, but the system-level rule is as stated.
